title: Your first join
prompt: Show each order's id and the name of its customer. Replace the ___ with the join condition.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT orders.id, customers.name FROM orders JOIN customers ON customers.id = orders.customer_id;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT orders.id, customers.name FROM orders JOIN customers ON customers.id = orders.id;
wrongSolutions.why: Matches on the order's own id

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT orders.id, customers.name FROM orders JOIN customers;
wrongSolutions.why: Pairs every order with every customer

title: Who ordered what
prompt: Show each order's item along with the name of the customer who placed it. Leave out orders that don't match a known customer.
hints: orders.customer_id points to customers.id. Connect them with JOIN ... ON.

cases.name: Different orders
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (5, 'Lena'), (6, 'Omar'); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (9, 6, 'Mocha', 5.0), (10, 8, 'Toast', 2.5);

solutions: SELECT customers.name, orders.item FROM orders JOIN customers ON customers.id = orders.customer_id;
SELECT c.name, o.item FROM customers c INNER JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT customers.name, orders.item FROM orders LEFT JOIN customers ON customers.id = orders.customer_id;
wrongSolutions.why: Keeps an order with no known customer

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT customers.name, orders.item FROM orders JOIN customers;
wrongSolutions.why: Pairs every order with every customer

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT customers.name, orders.item FROM orders JOIN customers ON customers.id = orders.id;

title: Using aliases
prompt: Show each employee's name and their department's name as department. Use the aliases e and d.
hints: FROM employees e JOIN departments d.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test');

solutions: SELECT e.name, d.name AS department FROM employees e JOIN departments d ON d.id = e.department_id;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT e.name, e.name AS department FROM employees e JOIN departments d ON d.id = e.department_id;
SELECT e.name, d.name AS department FROM employees e JOIN departments d ON d.id = e.id;

title: Who's enrolled
prompt: Show each enrolment's grade and the name of its student.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM enrolments; DELETE FROM courses; DELETE FROM students; INSERT INTO students VALUES (6, 'Femi', 9), (7, 'Gia', 9), (8, 'Hao', 10); INSERT INTO courses VALUES (5, 'Chemistry', 'Science'), (6, 'Drama', 'Arts'); INSERT INTO enrolments VALUES (11, 6, 5, 60, '2023-autumn'), (12, 6, 5, 60, '2024-spring'), (13, 7, 5, NULL, '2024-spring'), (14, 7, 6, 95, '2024-spring');

solutions: SELECT s.name, e.grade FROM enrolments e JOIN students s ON s.id = e.student_id;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT s.name, e.grade FROM enrolments e JOIN students s ON s.id = e.course_id;
SELECT e.student_id, e.grade FROM enrolments e;

title: Unmatched rows vanish
prompt: Show each customer's name and order item. Orders pointing to an unknown customer and customers with no orders won't appear. This is how an inner join behaves.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (5, 'Lena'), (6, 'Omar'), (8, 'Zuri'); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (9, 6, 'Mocha', 5.0), (10, 9, 'Toast', 2.5), (11, 6, 'Bun', 1.5);

solutions: SELECT c.name, o.item FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT c.name, o.item FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id;
SELECT c.name, o.item FROM orders o LEFT JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.id;

title: Fix the missing link
prompt: This should show each order item's product name and quantity, but it gives far too many rows. Fix it.
hints: The join has no condition, so every row pairs with every product.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT p.name, i.quantity FROM order_items i JOIN products p ON p.id = i.product_id;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT p.name, i.quantity FROM order_items i JOIN products p ON p.id = i.order_id;
SELECT i.product_id, i.quantity FROM order_items i;

title: Line value
prompt: Show each order item's order_id, the product name, and price times quantity as line_value.
hints: Calculate using columns from both tables.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT i.order_id, p.name, p.price * i.quantity AS line_value FROM order_items i JOIN products p ON p.id = i.product_id;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT i.order_id, p.name, p.price AS line_value FROM order_items i JOIN products p ON p.id = i.product_id;
SELECT i.order_id, p.name, p.cost * i.quantity AS line_value FROM order_items i JOIN products p ON p.id = i.product_id;

title: Revenue per category
prompt: Show each product category and its total revenue as revenue, using price times quantity, highest first. Include every order, whatever its status.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT p.category, SUM(p.price * i.quantity) AS revenue FROM order_items i JOIN products p ON p.id = i.product_id GROUP BY p.category ORDER BY revenue DESC;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT p.category, SUM(p.price) AS revenue FROM order_items i JOIN products p ON p.id = i.product_id GROUP BY p.category ORDER BY revenue DESC;
SELECT p.category, SUM(p.price * i.quantity) AS revenue FROM order_items i JOIN products p ON p.id = i.product_id GROUP BY p.category ORDER BY revenue;
